stem: In medieval Europe, lords often made peasants ____ on their land for several days each week.
explanation: In the active voice, "make" + object is followed by the base form of the verb: "made peasants work."

stem: Many national parks do not let visitors ____ the wild animals.
explanation: "Let" + object is followed by the base form: "let visitors feed." "Let" is never followed by "to."

stem: The museum had the ancient manuscript ____ by experts before putting it on display.
explanation: When the object receives the action, "have" + object is followed by the past participle: "had the ancient manuscript examined by experts."

stem: Advertising campaigns in the 1920s got many Americans ____ products on credit.
explanation: "Get" + person is followed by the to-infinitive: "got many Americans to buy products."

stem: The scientist had her assistants ____ the temperature of the samples every hour.
explanation: "Have" + person is followed by the base form: "had her assistants record the temperature."

stem: City officials {0} engineers {1} the old bridge carefully before {2} it {3} traffic.
explanation: "Have" + person is followed by the base form, not the to-infinitive: "had engineers inspect the old bridge."
In the active voice, "make" + object is followed by the base form: "make even tall trees sway."

stem: Before the printing press {0} invented, wealthy readers {1} {2} books {3} by hand.
explanation: When the object receives the action, "have" + object is followed by the past participle: "had their books copied by hand."

stem: Wealthy merchants in Renaissance Italy often had their portraits {0} by {1} artists, {2} were {3} paid.
explanation: The portraits receive the action, so "have" + object is followed by the past participle: "had their portraits painted."

stem: The yearly flooding of the Nile {0} ancient Egyptian {1} {2} crops in soil {3} was rich in nutrients.
explanation: "Let" + object is followed by the base form without "to": "let ancient Egyptian farmers grow crops."
